players.product: inspection & metrology for HBM / 2.5D advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2 revenue of $133.2 million, up 8% year over year and 10% sequentially and above guidance. Non-GAAP gross margin was 51.4%, operating expenses $32.5 million (up from $30.9 million, mainly R&D including resources from the Visual Layer acquisition), operating profit $36 million for a 27% operating margin versus 25.5% in Q1, and net income $39.4 million or $0.78 per diluted share on 51.5 million shares. Asia accounted for 92% of revenue. Approximately 75% of revenue came from ADVANCED PACKAGING, with the majority supporting AI-related applications.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $133.2M (+8% YoY, +10% QoQ); gross margin 51.4%; operating margin 27%; EPS $0.78; ~75% of revenue from advanced packaging

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance is $158-160 million, an exceptional 20% sequential increase, with sequential double-digit growth again in Q4. Second-half 2026 revenue is expected to be MORE THAN 30% above the first half, followed by continued growth into 2027. Profitability targets: gross margin of 52.5% to 53% exiting the year (from 51.4% in Q2) and operating margin of 30% to 32% by the end of the year, driven by mix toward the higher-ASP Eagle G5 and Hawk platforms plus operating leverage, with operating expense growth deliberately lagging revenue growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $158M-$160M (+20% QoQ); H2 2026 >30% above H1; GM 52.5-53% and operating margin 30-32% exiting the year

quarterly_data.signal: Order intake has accelerated sharply: MORE THAN $600 MILLION of orders received year to date, with deliveries scheduled through the remainder of 2026 and into 2027, materially improving visibility well into 2027. Approximately 80% of those orders are advanced packaging applications. OSATs accounted for MORE THAN 50% of total order intake, HBM players for OVER 20% of the $600 million (against the $260 million of POs and forecasts discussed on the prior call), and photonics for about 5%. Order flow started in Q1 and has grown steadily since. Most orders now being received are for 2027 rather than 2026, and management says a nice 2027 backlog is already building, with additional 2027 OSAT orders already in discussion.
quarterly_data.figure: >$600M orders year to date; ~80% advanced packaging; OSATs >50% of intake; HBM >20%; photonics ~5%

quarterly_data.signal: The HBM4 transition is a direct order driver: CEO Rafi Amit said 'the industry transition to HBM4 together with continued capacity expansion has resulted in significant orders from MULTIPLE LEADING HBM MANUFACTURERS.' In parallel, ongoing expansion of 2.5D and 3D IC packaging capacity is producing large multi-system orders from leading foundries, IDMs and OSATs. Within the HPC/AI portion of the business the two main segments are HBM and CoWoS (and CoWoS-like) applications, both expanding quickly and growing at roughly similar pace, with the faster one depending on which customers add capacity. Growth is attributed to a combination of share gains and genuine market capacity additions across HBM, CoWoS, fan-in and fan-out.

Advanced packaging mix is stepping up through the year: it was approximately 75% of Q2 revenue and is expected to reach around 80% by Q4. The advanced packaging business is expected to grow approximately 45% in the second half versus the first half, and Q4 advanced packaging revenue is expected to be approximately 70% HIGHER THAN Q1. HPC and AI-related products are already around 55% of revenue and may reach closer to 60% by the end of the year, with conventional advanced packaging roughly another 20%. Non-advanced-packaging business is stable with modest growth, helped by significant CMOS image sensor orders and early signs of recovery in consumer-related areas.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced packaging ~75% of Q2 revenue rising to ~80% by Q4; AP +45% H2 vs H1; Q4 AP ~70% above Q1; HPC/AI ~55% of revenue rising toward ~60%

quarterly_data.signal: New platforms are carrying the mix: the Eagle G5 and Hawk generated approximately 50% of systems revenue in Q2, with contribution expected to keep rising as adoption accelerates, and they lift ASPs. Hawk targets high-volume, high-end applications - HBM is cited as the example where Camtek is selling more Hawks - and combined with new AI technology is enabling penetration into additional process steps INCLUDING HYBRID BONDING. Eagle G5 offers better resolution, optics, throughput and cost of ownership, and existing Eagle customers are switching to it. Camtek is also launching NanoProf, a new metrology platform built on the FRT business acquired three years ago plus Camtek-developed technology, installed at selected customers from Q1 and covering wafer topography, shape and bow. Additional new modules include a high-resolution backside inspection module and fluorescence illumination for detecting organic residue. Further detail is promised at an investor breakfast at SEMICON West on October 14, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Eagle G5 + Hawk ~50% of Q2 systems revenue; NanoProf metrology platform launching; hybrid bonding process steps being addressed

quarterly_data.signal: Photonics is emerging as a new growth market: Camtek has already received multi-system orders from several customers and expects photonics to become an important contributor in coming years. It represented about 5% of the more than $600 million of year-to-date orders and is expected to exceed that share in 2027. The two main segments are SILICON PHOTONICS, where Camtek has already sold a number of machines, and COMPOUND SEMICONDUCTORS covering the various diodes used for transceivers and receivers.
quarterly_data.figure: Photonics ~5% of the >$600M of year-to-date orders, expected higher in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Camtek says it is successfully managing the operational challenge of unprecedented demand: it expanded production capacity and strengthened its supply chain well in advance, has all subcontractors and supply chain in place, and COO Ramy Langer said there are no issues or obstacles regarding capacity and the company is confident of shipping machines on time. It is now further expanding manufacturing capacity, system integration capability, the sales organisation and customer support infrastructure to support substantially higher annual revenue levels. Inventory was flat in Q2 but is expected to grow in coming quarters to support forecast revenue growth.

Region and balance sheet: China was 49% of revenue last year and is expected at around the mid-40s percent this year as other regions grow faster, with the China business itself described as stable and continuing to invest in semiconductors. Cash, cash equivalents, short- and long-term deposits and marketable securities were $815.8 million at June 30, 2026. Cash generated from operations was $12.2 million in the quarter. Accounts receivable rose to $153.9 million from $131.7 million on higher business volume, taking DSO to 105 days. Financial income was $7 million, down from $8.1 million, mainly on devaluation of balance sheet items from a weaker U.S. dollar against the Israeli shekel.
quarterly_data.figure: China ~mid-40s% of 2026 revenue (from 49%); cash and investments $815.8M; Q2 cash from operations $12.2M
